expenditures.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE = 860.00 on the p2 SUMMARY PAGE (restated at line 6), which is also Schedule B's own printed 'Subtotal for this page $ 860.00' and its printed 'Total Expenditures Received (Sum of subtotals from all Schedule B pages) $ 860.00' — a heading the filer corrected by hand, writing 'Made' beneath the printed word 'Received'
expenditures.detail: 4 Schedule B entries sum to 300.00 + 60.00 + 125.00 + 375.00 = 860.00 exactly = the schedule's page subtotal = the schedule's own total = the cover's promoted per-period Column A cell = line 6. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' prints 16,854.71 and is retained as cumulative, never summed. Each entry occupies TWO printed rows (payee and amount on the odd row, purpose on the even row, address across both), so the four entries sit on printed rows 1, 3, 5 and 7 and rows 2, 4, 6, 8 carry no amount — the continuation rows print a BARE DASH in the date and amount cells, which under the zero-glyph ruling is a nil mark and NOT a numeral, so no phantom zero-value rows are created from them.

in_kind_convention: MONETARY-PLUS-IN-KIND on the contribution side — tested both ways before the verdict. Schedule A row 1 is annotated by the filer, in his own hand beside the figure, as '$60.00 - (In kind donation)', and that 60.00 is INSIDE the schedule's own printed 310.00 subtotal: monetary-only gives 250.00 against a stated 310.00 and fails by exactly 60.00, while monetary-plus-in-kind closes to the cent. The expenditure side needs no such test — its four entries carry no in-kind marking and sum to the stated 860.00 as cash — but note that the SAME 60.00 web-hosting fee appears on BOTH sides (as an in-kind donation from IT Solutions LLC and as a web-hosting expenditure to the same vendor over the same date range), which is the standard in-kind double entry and a second 2014 instance of the pattern Lee's filing shows. In-kind treatment remains per FILER, and this filer books it inline.

A FILER CORRECTING THE COUNTY'S OWN PRINTED HEADING: at the foot of Schedule B he writes 'Made' underneath the printed words 'Total Expenditures Received', fixing the county's wording — the companion to ADDENDUM B §B5's 2012 filer who struck 'Contributor' and wrote 'Payee'. BARE DASHES sit in the date and amount cells of every continuation row on Schedule B — nil marks, not numerals, so they create no rows and no zeros.
